_about: The rule document a repair cites (rules/repair.py). A construct cannot heal on its own
(Bestiary, Construct type: 'Cannot heal damage on its own, but often can be repaired
... through the use of the Craft Construct feat. Constructs can also be healed through
spells such as make whole.'), so the hit points a mended machine gets back are this
row's dice, rolled by the engine and stamped rule:<id> — never a number the plan wrote.
Every field is the book's except where a field says HOUSE.

repair-construct.name: repairing a construct
repair-construct.source: Ultimate Magic p.113, Repairing Constructs (aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=979): 'a crafter can repair a construct with the Craft Construct feat. When repairing a construct, its master spends 100 gp per Hit Die of the construct, and then makes a skill check as if he were crafting the construct with a DC of 5 less than the DC for crafting that construct. With a success, the construct regains 1d6 hit points per Hit Die of the construct. Completing a repair takes 1 day per 1,000 gp spent on the repair (minimum of 1 day). Repair in this way can only be performed while the construct is inanimate or nonfunctioning.' And: 'A construct that has been completely destroyed cannot be repaired, though at the GM's option some of the materials may be usable in the construction of a new construct.'
repair-construct.crafting_dc_house: HOUSE, used only when the stat block prints no construction DC: the Core Rulebook's Craft table puts a 'complex or superior item (lock)' at DC 20. The Clockwork Spy's own printed construction line is Craft (clockwork) DC 20 (Bestiary 3), so for it this is the book's number.
